Create setting for Iterative Hard Thresholding model

Source: R/CyclopsSettings.R
setIterativeHardThresholding.Rd

Logistic regression with K non-zero coefficients, fitted with the IterativeHardThresholding package (version 2.0.0 or later). It maximizes the log-likelihood minus a small ridge penalty (variance) over models with K covariates. When K or variance has several values, the hyperparameter search chooses between them on the training folds, as for other models, by the held-out log-likelihood unless the hyperparameter settings name another tuningMetric. Each fold's training rows are converted to Cyclops data once, and each fold starts a candidate from its own fit at the nearest earlier one (the next smaller K). The foldWorkers of createHyperparameterSettings() fit the folds in parallel.

Usage

setIterativeHardThresholding(
  K = 25,
  variance = 1,
  exclude = c(),
  forceIntercept = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  algorithm = "default",
  control = list(),
  oneStandardError = FALSE,
  threads = -1,
  ...
)

Arguments

K

Number of covariates in the model (default 25, or 10 with algorithm = "legacy", as in earlier versions); the intercept and exclude do not count. With fewer covariates than K, the model has all of them. One whole number, or several to choose from by cross-validation, for example c(5, 10, 25, 50, 100), which takes several times longer to fit.

variance

Ridge variance (default 1): a positive number, Inf for plain L0 (the best subset of size K), several numbers to choose from by cross-validation, or "tune" for the grid 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3 and Inf. In earlier versions the second argument was penalty, so give variance by name; given by position, it gives a warning.

exclude

Covariate ids (numbers) that are not penalized and do not count towards K.

forceIntercept

Logical: penalize the intercept and count it towards K.

seed

An option to add a seed when training the model.

algorithm

"default", "chu2020" (the algorithm of Chu et al., 2020) or "legacy" (IterativeHardThresholding 1.0.3: Broken Adaptive Ridge with at most K covariates, counting the intercept; deprecated, to reproduce earlier models).

control

A named list of algorithm switches; see IterativeHardThresholding::createIhtControl(). Empty entries take the defaults of algorithm.

oneStandardError

With several K: choose the smallest K whose held-out log-likelihood is within one standard error of the best. This gives smaller models, which can discriminate less well than the best K.

threads

Kept for earlier code; not used. The refits run on control$threads threads (default 1); to fit the folds in parallel, use createHyperparameterSettings(foldWorkers = ).

...

Only with algorithm = "legacy": the arguments of IterativeHardThresholding 1.0.3 (penalty, fitBestSubset, initialRidgeVariance, tolerance, maxIterations, threshold, delta).

Value

modelSettings object

References

Chu BB, Keys KL, German CA, Zhou H, Zhou JJ, Sobel EM, Sinsheimer JS, Lange K (2020). Iterative hard thresholding in genome-wide association studies: Generalized linear models, prior weights, and double sparsity. GigaScience 9(6), giaa044.

Examples

modelIht <- setIterativeHardThresholding(K = 5, seed = 42)
# choose K by cross-validation
modelIht <- setIterativeHardThresholding(K = c(10, 25, 50), seed = 42)
